Loads a model together with its parts and animation. The result is a pivot at the top of a hierarchy of entities, one per object in the file (and per light and camera, for `.3ds`), so you can find a single part with [FindChild](FindChild) and play the animation with `Animate`. Unlike [LoadMesh](LoadMesh) the parts stay separate entities, which costs more to draw but lets them move.
@returns The handle of the top entity, or 0 if the file could not be loaded.
@param file    Path of the model file.
@param parent  Entity the model follows, or 0 for none. Defaults to 0.
@gap Models in `.b3d`, `.3ds` and DirectX `.x` files can be loaded, see [LoadMesh](LoadMesh). A DirectX `.x` file brings its frames as entities and the animation keys of its animation sets, see [DirectX models](DirectX-Models). A `.3ds` file brings its object hierarchy, keys, lights and cameras (a light is a light entity, a camera is a pivot that looks at its target), see [3D Studio models](3D-Studio-Models). A glTF 2.0 file (`.gltf` or `.glb`) brings its nodes as entities, its skins and its animations, see [glTF models](glTF-Models).
